name: Shell
description: Run finite shell commands or retain command sessions with bounded output, stdin and optional PTY on the active platform.

executeCommand.description: Execute a command in the active platform shell and return the result.
executeCommand.progressive_guidance: This tool waits for command completion and returns output and exit status; longRunning only extends the timeout. Prefer it for short finite tasks whose result is needed next. Use startSession for long checks, downloads and installs so owner follow-ups do not discard running work. Batch independent commands in one turn. Bash commands use ordinary exit-status semantics; fail-fast behavior requires an explicit set -e. Use && for dependent operations and test optional programs/files in if conditions so expected absence is reported without aborting an inventory scan. The final command determines the exit status unless the script exits explicitly; nonzero status is reported with captured stdout and stderr. For existing background work, check its result before waiting again. Use startSession for interactive or persistent commands, or to overlap a long command with independent work. Ordinary commands remain isolated and do not share a session shell or its environment. Keep stdout and stderr attached to the tool for progress.

longRunning.description: Set true only for commands expected to run for a long time. Uses a deterministic 24-hour timeout.

startSession.description: Start a retained command and immediately return a conversation-owned sessionId. Streams live output and completion to the app; supports stdin and optional PTY.
startSession.progressive_guidance: Use for long checks, downloads, installs, dev servers, watchers and interactive commands so owner follow-ups can be handled while work continues. Prefer executeCommand for short finite tasks to avoid a separate launch and status check. Keep stdout and stderr attached so progress streams to the app; do not redirect them to a log file to hide the running command output. Supply the observed project cwd. Use pipes by default, pty=true only when a TTY is needed. This starts one command, not a shared shell for later executeCommand calls. A successful start is not a passed check: inspect running, exitCode and commandSucceeded. Retain sessionId and command in the plan; use readSession after follow-ups or interruptions before deciding whether a restart is needed. Informational questions preserve running sessions; stop affected sessions on cancellation or a redirect that makes their work inapplicable. Stop owned sessions when the task finishes unless asked to keep them running. A worker restart loses live sessions; inspect before restarting commands.

timeoutMs.description: Total command lifetime, not a launch or read wait. Omit for the default 24-hour lifetime of persistent/interactive commands; stop the session when finished.

readSession.description: Read bounded retained command output and its current process status using an absolute character cursor.
readSession.progressive_guidance: Use only a sessionId returned by startSession in this conversation. Follow nextOffsetChars; hasMore means another saved output page is available. outputLost means the requested cursor predates the retained tail. running=true is unfinished work. Reconcile exitCode, signal and commandSucceeded before reporting a completed check. Reads return immediately; avoid repeated empty polling when independent work can proceed.

writeSession.description: Send bounded stdin to a running command owned by this conversation. Newlines must be included explicitly.
writeSession.progressive_guidance: Inspect the current prompt before answering. Include a newline when submitting a line. Input can cause side effects and must stay within the authorized task; command launch checks are not a sandbox for later input. Never send owner passwords or secrets through agent stdin. Use stopSession to terminate the command rather than assuming control characters stopped its descendants.

stopSession.description: Stop the owned command and its descendants, retaining final output and termination status.
stopSession.progressive_guidance: Stop only sessions belonging to the current task. Inspect running=false in the returned result before claiming cleanup. Stopped or timed-out commands are not successful checks. Completed sessions can still be read until evicted or their worker shuts down.
